headline: Employment of 90.0 % is close to the benchmarks, with full-time work matching them almost exactly.
how_to_read: Flows run from all respondents (left) to employed or not employed (middle) and then to detailed situation (right); width is the share of respondents. The hatched "Hidden" flow marks details held back because fewer than 3 people fall into them.
key_findings: Employed graduates account for 90.0 %, of whom 75.0 % work full-time and 10.0 % are self-employed.
The 10.0 % not employed contain no students, retirees or other situations; seeking work and not seeking work are hidden.
benchmark: Employment is 1.3 pp below Asia (91.3 %) and 2.6 pp below all schools (92.6 %). Full-time work is within 0.4 pp of Asia (74.6 %), while self-employment is 2.0 pp above all schools (8.0 %).
caveats: At n = 40 one person still moves the percentages by a couple of points; part-time, other employment, seeking work and not seeking work are hidden (fewer than 3 people).
